title: Review your insurance and subscriptions with an agent
summary: An X user says their 'CFO' bot reviewed home and auto insurance, emailed and negotiated with their insurance agent, and flagged unused subscriptions, saving $2,822 a year.
agent_role: The bot reviewed home and auto insurance and monthly subscriptions, then emailed the user's insurance agent and negotiated. The post does not say how much the user supervised.
outcome: The author reports saving $2,822 per year.
what_they_did: The poster set up a bot they call their CFO. It did a full review of their home and auto insurance. It emailed their insurance agent and negotiated a better deal. It also went through their monthly subscriptions to find ones they weren't using.
how_it_went: The poster says the bot saved them $2,822 a year.
prompt: Act as my personal finance assistant. Review my current home and auto insurance policies [attach policy documents] and my monthly subscriptions [attach bank or card statements]. List each subscription with its cost and when I last used it, and flag ones I seem not to use. For insurance, summarize my coverage and price, and draft a polite email to my insurance agent [agent's email] asking for a lower rate or better options. Show me the draft and the list of subscriptions to cancel, and wait for my approval before sending anything or cancelling any service.

curation.rationale: A real multi-step finance task: reviewing insurance, emailing the insurance agent and checking subscriptions, with a dollar figure. Very thin on details and framed as a reply asking for attention, so only just publishable.
